## What this is
::: {.cgp-panel}

```{ojs}
aboutHeader = html`<div>
  <p class="cgp-notice">Built ${meta.built_at_utc} from capture ${meta.capture_id}.
    Data: <a href=${meta.releases.current}>current release</a> ·
    <a href=${meta.releases.all}>all releases</a> ·
    <a href="https://github.com/coatless-data/club-gas-prices#schema-capture-grain-in-file-order">column
    reference</a>.</p>
</div>`
```

Prices are read from each chain's own public website every four hours while a
station is open, and stored by UTC day. Every row keeps the published value, its
unit, and the exchange rate in force when it was collected, so a past day shows
the USD value of that day.

| Country | Endpoint, one request unless noted |
|---|---|
| United States | `ecom-api.costco.com/core/warehouse-locator/v1/warehouses.json` for metadata, then `www.costco.com/AjaxGetGasPricesService?warehouseid=…` in batches of 10 |
| Canada | `www.costco.ca/AjaxWarehouseBrowseLookupView?hasGas=true&populateWarehouseDetails=true&countryCode=CA` |
| Mexico | `www.costco.com.mx/rest/v2/mexico/stores?fields=FULL&…` |
| United Kingdom | `www.costco.co.uk/rest/v2/uk/stores?fields=FULL&…` |
| Australia | `www.costco.com.au/rest/v2/australia/stores?fields=FULL&…` |
| Japan | `www.costco.co.jp/rest/v2/japan/stores?fields=FULL&…` |
| Taiwan | `www.costco.com.tw/rest/v2/taiwan/stores?fields=FULL&…` |

:::

## Grades
::: {.cgp-panel}

```{ojs}
aboutGrades = html`<table class="cgp-table">
  <thead><tr><th>Country</th><th>Chain</th><th>Source label</th><th>Grade</th>
    <th>Spec</th><th>Stated by</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>${(meta.grades || []).map(
    (row) => html`<tr>
      <td>${COUNTRY_NAMES[row.country] || row.country}</td>
      <td>${BRAND_NAMES[row.brand] || row.brand || ""}</td>
      <td>${row.grade_raw}</td>
      <td>${row.grade}</td>
      <td>${row.spec || "—"}</td>
      <td>${
        row.spec_source
          ? row.spec_source_url
            ? html`<a href=${row.spec_source_url}>${row.spec_source}</a>`
            : row.spec_source
          : "—"
      }</td>
    </tr>`
  )}</tbody>
</table>`
```

Grades are not equivalent across countries. UK and Australian diesel is premium
diesel, and these are one chain's posted prices, not national averages. Where a
source states no octane or blend the specification is blank; where it comes from
a third party it is marked `reported` and links to that source.

:::


## Units, rates and caveats
::: {.cgp-panel}

**Units.** One US gallon is 3.785411784 litres. UK prices are published in
pence, so `GBp/L` is divided by 100 for the pound figure. Puerto Rico's prices
are published in USD per litre: #335 regular was 1.097, about 4.15 per gallon,
and Puerto Rico retail is priced per litre. That unit is inferred, not stated.

**Exchange rates.** Each capture fetches the daily reference rate from
Frankfurter v2 and stores it with every row. If that fails, a dated
`@fawazahmed0/currency-api` file is used; if that also fails, the most recent
stored rate within 7 days is carried forward and labelled
`carried-forward:<source>`. If no rate is available the USD columns are null:
those stations are drawn gray on the map, show their local price only, and are
left out of USD aggregates.

**Filtering.** Placeholder prices are dropped: stations that price before they
open (the pre-opening 3.999 / 5.999 pattern in the United States, and Canadian
warehouses with no gas hours), premium-only business-center placeholders, and
values outside per-unit sanity bounds.

**How fresh a price really is.** A capture records when *we* read a price, not
when the retailer changed it. The United Kingdom's store feed is served with a
90-minute cache, and a re-request 73 seconds later returned a byte-identical
response, so a UK price can be up to about an hour and a half old however often
this runs. Every country's feed is a published figure rather than a live reading
from the pump.

**UTC days versus local time.** Days are UTC days. For Japan, Taiwan and
Australia the last capture of a UTC day arrives early the next local morning, so
`local_date` in the released rows can be a day ahead of `capture_date`.

**Known limits.** No source publishes a price timestamp, prices change during
the day, and the storefront APIs declare CDN caching of up to 90 minutes. Costco
prices are not national averages.

:::

aboutAttribution = {
